newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-INJURIES CLOUD NEW ZEALAND-AUSTRALIA CLASH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-INJURIES CLOUD NEW ZEALAND-AUSTRALIA CLASH.

text.p: Injury concerns have clouded the build-up to the first clash of the season between New Zealand and Australia in Christchurch on Saturday.
Both sides come off convincing 2-0 wins in their respective preparation series -- the Wallabies beat five-nations champions France and the All Blacks completely demolished Argentina.
But the loss of key players through injury has muted their confidence heading into this crunch match, the first of three Bledisloe Cup tests between the trans-Tasman rivals.

Australia are banking on three injured players returning to fitness and have named only one newcomer in their side. Rookie lock Matt Cockbain comes in for David Giffin, who has been ruled out with a broken foot.

Dynamic centre Jason Little, wing Ben Tune and flanker David Wilson are all carrying injuries but have been included in Australia's starting 15. Coach Greg Smith said Daniel Herbert, Mitch Hardy and Daniel Manu are on standby, with Herbert the most likely to start if Little fails to recover from his hip injury in time.
For the All Blacks, linchpin Andrew Mehrtens has failed to fully recover from a hamstring strain -- although the Wallabies won't take much comfort from his replacement.
Dashing fly-half Carlos Spencer, fresh from a 53-point haul in just two tests against Argentina, will play his third consecutive test in Mehrtens' absence.

Although New Zealand have fewer injury woes than Australia, All Black coach John Hart believes the ease with which his team vanquished Argentina has left them under prepared for what he said was their most important test of the year.

"The preparation we've had is nowhere near what we were looking for. I think we are considerably underdone versus Australia, who have had two games against France," he said. "So that's a worry coming into this test."
Hart said the first clash between New Zealand and Australia was the first of many tough encounters for both teams, and it was psychologically a crucial match to win.
"It's really important that we play well this weekend to give ourselves the confidence to go into what's a difficult programme ahead," he said.
"So it is a very, very important test."

Hart took little pleasure from the Wallabies' injury woes, saying they had excellent replacement players to draw on. But one man Australia may miss is full-back Matthew Burke, who has yet to recover from the groin strain which sidelined him for the tests against the French.
The less experienced Stephen Larkham plays opposite All Black full-back Christian Cullen, who has been more than living up to his star billing with his devastating recent form.

The Wallaby forwards will also need to put in a strong performance to challenge the All Black tight five who have looked ominous in their matches this year. Last year, the All Blacks soundly beat the Wallabies 43-6 in their first Bledisloe Cup clash.

Australia - 15-Stephen Larkham; 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-Pat Howard, 11-Joe Roff; 10-Tim Horan, 9-George Gregan; 8-Troy Coker, 7-David Wilson, 6-Brett Robinson, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Matt Cockbain, 3-Ewen McKenzie, 2-Marco Caputo, 1-Richard Harry.

New Zealand - 15-Christian Cullen, 14-Jeff Wilson, 13-Frank Bunce, 12-Lee Stensness 11-Tana Umaga; 10-Carlos Spencer, 9-Justin Marshall, 8-Zinzan Brooke, 7-Josh Kronfeld, 6-Taine Randell, 5-Ian Jones, 4-Robin Brooke, 3-Craig Dowd, 2-Sean Fitzpatrick (captain), 1-Olo Brown.
